title: M19. Compositional security against super-rushing
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Give a useful composable security definition and composition theorem for super-rushing protocols, identifying sufficient causal and state-isolation conditions.
status: The 2025 work shows that even sequential composition can fail to preserve super-rushing security.
why: Individually secure subprotocols must remain secure when assembled into larger workflows.
key_works: Asharov–Chandramouli–Cohen–Ishai (2025), [*Peeking Into the Future*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1394); Canetti (2001), [*Universally Composable Security: A New Paradigm for Cryptographic Protocols*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2000/067).

title: M21. Complete fairness classification for asymmetric Boolean functionalities
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Characterize exactly which two-party functionalities with potentially different Boolean outputs admit complete fairness, through an effectively checkable criterion and matching constructions or impossibilities.
status: Symmetric Boolean functionalities were classified in 2015. The asymmetric extension and 2017 construction framework leave unresolved cases.
why: Identifies when fairness is possible without an honest majority or trusted intervention.
key_works: Asharov–Beimel–Makriyannis–Omri (2015), [*Complete Characterization of Fairness in Secure Two-Party Computation of Boolean Functions*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/1000); Daza–Makriyannis (2017), [*Designing Fully Secure Protocols for Secure Two-Party Computation of Constant-Domain Functions*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/098).

title: M22. Fairness classification beyond Boolean outputs
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Find necessary and sufficient conditions for complete fairness of arbitrary finite-output deterministic and randomized two-party functionalities.
status: Boolean classifications, constant-domain constructions, and reductions to fair coin tossing provide partial structure, without a universal classification.
why: Auctions, exchanges, and private analytics produce richer outputs than a shared bit.
key_works: Daza–Makriyannis (2017), [*Designing Fully Secure Protocols for Secure Two-Party Computation of Constant-Domain Functions*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/098); Asharov–Lindell–Rabin (2013), [*Full Characterization of Functions that Imply Fair Coin Tossing and Ramifications to Fairness*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/110).

title: M23. Fairness with a growing dishonest majority
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Characterize efficiently realizable fair symmetric Boolean function families when \(n=\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)\) and corruption exceeds \(n/2\) by a growing amount.
status: Dachman-Soled obtains broad families at \(n/2\) corruption and majority at \(n/2+c\) for fixed constants \(c\); growing surplus remains distinct.
why: Could identify useful collective decisions remaining fair despite substantial collusion.
key_works: Dachman-Soled (2020), [*Revisiting Fairness in MPC: Polynomial Number of Parties and General Adversarial Structures*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1430).

title: M24. Exact cryptographic strength of a small trusted intervention
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Characterize assumptions necessary and sufficient for general fully secure MPC using a trusted party invoked once whose work is independent of circuit size.
status: The 2022 minimal-trust work gives succinct-FE constructions and lower bounds for restricted approaches; the unrestricted characterization remains open.
why: Determines how much advanced cryptography is needed to minimize trusted computation.
key_works: Ishai–Patra–Patranabis–Ravi–Srinivasan (2022), [*Fully-Secure MPC with Minimal Trust*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1248).

title: M28. Three-round plain-model ZK from polynomial hardness
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Construct three-message ordinary negligible-error ZK arguments for all NP from conventional polynomial hardness, eliminating the additional keyless multi-collision-resistant-hashing hypothesis.
status: Three-round ZK itself is established. Kiyoshima’s 2026 journal result uses LWE and keyless multi-collision resistance secure against slightly superpolynomial adversaries.
why: Identifies the assumption cost of crossing classical black-box simulation barriers.
key_works: Kiyoshima (2026), [*Public-Coin Three-Round Zero-Knowledge from Learning with Errors and Keyless Multi-Collision-Resistant Hash*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00145-025-09551-8).

title: M29. Complexity-only lower bounds for three-round ZK proofs
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Rule out three-round negligible-error ZK proofs for NP using ordinary complexity separations while allowing non-black-box simulation.
status: The 2018 impossibility uses program-obfuscation assumptions. Three-round computationally sound arguments do not settle the proof question.
why: Would distinguish intrinsic interaction limits from consequences of powerful cryptographic assumptions.
key_works: Fleischhacker–Goyal–Jain (2018), [*On the Existence of Three Round Zero-Knowledge Proofs*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2018/167).

title: M30. Four-round ZK proofs with non-black-box simulation
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Determine whether NP admits four-message negligible-error ZK proofs with code-aware simulation, using a conventional assumption or a matching lower bound.
status: Five-round proofs are known; four-round black-box proofs face lower bounds. Existing three-round impossibilities leave this boundary distinct.
why: Tests whether inspecting verifier code can save a round while retaining unconditional soundness.
key_works: Katz (2008), [*Which Languages Have 4-Round Zero-Knowledge Proofs?*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-78524-8_5); Fleischhacker–Goyal–Jain (2018), [*On the Existence of Three Round Zero-Knowledge Proofs*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2018/167).

title: M32. Constant-round concurrent ZK from ordinary OWFs
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Construct constant-round concurrent ZK for NP from arbitrary polynomially secure OWFs in the plain model, with ordinary polynomial-time simulation.
status: OWF-based concurrent protocols and stronger-assumption constant-round protocols exist; the combined target remains open.
why: Would provide low-latency concurrent privacy from the basic symmetric-cryptography assumption.
key_works: Chung–Lin–Pass (2015), [*Constant-Round Concurrent Zero-Knowledge from Indistinguishability Obfuscation*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/991); Pass (2021), [*A Tutorial on Concurrent Zero Knowledge*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2021/615).

title: M34. Four-round statistical nonmalleable ZK from weaker assumptions
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Obtain four-round statistical nonmalleable ZK for NP from arbitrary OWFs, preserving negligible errors and delayed-input one-many simulation extractability.
status: Kiyoshima’s 2025 result, revised in 2026, achieves the target security properties from CRH and injective OWFs.
why: Would combine statistical privacy, low interaction, and minimal assumptions.
key_works: Kiyoshima (2025/2026), [*Four-round Statistical Non-malleable Zero-knowledge*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1787); Kiyoshima (2020), [*Statistical Concurrent Non-Malleable Zero-Knowledge from One-Way Functions*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00145-020-09348-x).

title: M37. Constant-round simultaneous resettability from OWFs
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Construct constant-round NP ZK that remains private under prover resets and sound under verifier resets, using only polynomially secure OWFs.
status: Simultaneous resettability from OWFs is known with polynomial rounds; constant-round constructions use stronger tools.
why: Would protect resettable devices without requiring obfuscation-scale assumptions.
key_works: Chung–Ostrovsky–Pass–Visconti (2013), [*Simultaneous Resettability from One-Way Functions*](https://www.cs.cornell.edu/~rafael/papers/focs13srzk.pdf); Chongchitmate–Ostrovsky–Visconti (2017), [*Resettably-Sound Resettable Zero Knowledge in Constant Rounds*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-70503-3_4).

title: M38. Low-overhead resettable statistical ZK
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Implement resettable statistical ZK with near-linear prover overhead from a specified witness-encryption instantiation, accounting for witness length, reset count, and security loss.
status: The 2024 equivalence between resettable statistical ZK arguments and witness encryption, assuming OWFs, is qualitative.
why: Would separate unavoidable assumption strength from avoidable implementation cost.
key_works: Kiyoshima (2024), [*Resettable Statistical Zero-Knowledge for NP*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/806).

title: M41. NIZK from arbitrary public-key encryption
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Construct reusable CRS-model NIZK arguments for NP from arbitrary semantically secure PKE, without assuming additional encryption structure or correlation-intractable hashing.
status: Long-standing. Recent constructions broaden concrete assumption families without establishing a generic CPA-PKE reduction.
why: Would show that noninteractive privacy requires no additional primitive beyond generic public-key confidentiality.
key_works: Branco et al. (2025), [*Black-Box Non-Interactive Zero Knowledge from Vector Trapdoor Hash*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1514); Dao–Jain–Jin (2024), [*Non-Interactive Zero-Knowledge from LPN and MQ*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1254).

title: M42. Fully black-box reusable NIZK from vector trapdoor hashing
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Upgrade vector-trapdoor-hash NIZKs to adaptive multi-theorem ZK while keeping the construction fully black-box in its cryptographic primitives.
status: The 2025 construction gives single-theorem black-box NIZK; its multi-theorem upgrade explicitly uses cryptography non-black-box.
why: Would retain modularity while supporting many proofs under one setup.
key_works: Branco–Choudhuri–Döttling–Jain–Malavolta–Srinivasan (2025/2026), [*Black-Box Non-Interactive Zero Knowledge from Vector Trapdoor Hash*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1514).

title: M43. Efficient-prover ZAPs from OWFs
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Construct two-message public-coin witness-indistinguishable proofs for NP from OWFs with a prover polynomial in instance and witness length.
status: Ball–Dachman-Soled obtain OWF-based ZAPs with prover time \(2^{n^\varepsilon}\) for every fixed positive \(\varepsilon\).
why: Would make minimal-assumption two-message proofs computationally usable.
key_works: Ball–Dachman-Soled (2023/2025), [*(Inefficient Prover) ZAPs from Hard-to-Invert Functions*](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2023/205/).

title: M44. Statistical ZAPs from polynomially hard LWE
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Construct two-message public-coin statistically witness-indistinguishable arguments from polynomially hard LWE, with polynomial modulus-to-noise ratio and negligible soundness error.
status: The 2025 hidden-bits construction obtains nonadaptive soundness using quasi-polynomial hardness.
why: Would remove a significant quantitative assumption penalty from compact statistical privacy.
key_works: Bradley–Lu–Nassar–Waters–Wu (2025), [*A Hidden-Bits Approach to Statistical ZAPs from LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1663).

title: M45. Adaptively sound statistical ZAPs without length-specific leverage
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Obtain adaptively sound statistical ZAPs for unrestricted polynomial statement lengths from polynomial or quasi-polynomial LWE hardness, without setup parameters tied to the largest future statement.
status: The 2025 construction obtains adaptive soundness under subexponential hardness for an a priori bounded statement length.
why: Long-lived public parameters should support statements chosen later.
key_works: Bradley–Lu–Nassar–Waters–Wu (2025), [*A Hidden-Bits Approach to Statistical ZAPs from LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1663).

title: M46. LPN-and-MQ NIZK without exponential MQ hardness
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Construct NP NIZK from polynomial hardness of ordinary LPN and random underdetermined multivariate quadratic equations, specifying whether privacy is computational or statistical.
status: Dao–Jain–Jin use polynomial LPN plus exponentially hard MQ for computational ZK; their statistical variant also uses dense-sparse LPN.
why: Would weaken the assumptions behind a non-LWE route to NIZK.
key_works: Dao–Jain–Jin (2024), [*Non-Interactive Zero-Knowledge from LPN and MQ*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1254).

title: M47. Statistical-privacy-preserving NIZK amplification
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Amplify nontrivial weak statistical NIZKs to negligible errors while preserving statistical privacy, using OWFs for proofs and PKE for arguments, without additional CRH.
status: Ordinary amplification is established under those respective assumptions; known preservation of statistical ZK and succinctness uses CRH.
why: Would preserve the strongest privacy guarantees while repairing weak security parameters.
key_works: Applebaum–Kachlon (2025), [*NIZK Amplification via Leakage-Resilient Secure Computation*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/995).

title: M49. Near-linear secret sharing of NP statements
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Achieve threshold NP-statement secret sharing with total transformed-instance size and computation \(\widetilde O(n(|x|+|w|)\operatorname{poly}(\lambda))\), retaining the full threshold range and required privacy.
status: All-threshold polynomial feasibility was established in 2025; the near-linear target is a stricter proposed refinement.
why: Would reduce the cost of distributing logical evidence and combining proof systems.
key_works: Applebaum–Kachlon (2025), [*How to Share an NP Statement or Combiners for Zero-Knowledge Proofs*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/334).

title: A02. General iO from one conventional pairing assumption
subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: Construct general iO from SXDH, DLIN, or another conventional pairing assumption alone, eliminating independent noisy-learning or coding assumptions.
status: Ragavan–Vafa–Vaikuntanathan’s 2024 construction uses DLIN plus large-field and sparse-binary LPN, while removing a separate local-PRG assumption.
why: Would simplify the logical foundation and cryptanalytic evaluation of obfuscation.
key_works: Ragavan–Vafa–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [*Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Bilinear Maps and LPN Variants*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/856).

title: A05. General iO from iPRO without extra algebraic assumptions
subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: Derive general iO from obfuscation for identical pseudorandom functions, iPRO, in the standard model without adding pairing assumptions.
status: The 2025 PRO work derives iO from iPRO plus pairings and stronger results from iPRO in a pseudorandom-oracle model.
why: Would clarify the exact power of a restricted obfuscation notion.
key_works: Branco–Döttling–Jain–Malavolta–Mathialagan–Peters–Vaikuntanathan (2024/2025), [*Pseudorandom Obfuscation and Applications*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1742).

title: A09. Exact source conditions for compute-and-compare obfuscation
subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: Characterize the weakest target unpredictability and auxiliary-information conditions supporting compute-and-compare obfuscation from polynomially secure LWE.
status: The 2017 construction covers broad sufficient-pseudoentropy regimes; matching positive and negative boundaries remain incomplete.
why: Applications differ sharply in how predictable their hidden comparison targets are.
key_works: Wichs–Zirdelis (2017), [*Obfuscating Compute-and-Compare Programs under LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/276).

title: A11. A 100-fold-overhead iO demonstrator
subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: Demonstrate proof-backed general iO with code size and evaluation time each within \(100\times\) baseline at a stated 128-bit classical security target, on a public circuit suite.
status: Proposed moonshot. Feasibility and quasilinear asymptotics do not establish this concrete envelope.
why: Would turn general obfuscation from a theoretical capability into an experimentally assessable technology.
key_works: Jain–Lin–Sahai (2020/2021), [*Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Well-Founded Assumptions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.09317); Ma–Dai–Shi (2025), [*Quasi-Linear Indistinguishability Obfuscation*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/307).

title: A13. Fully collusion-resistant circuit FE from ordinary LWE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Construct public-key FE for arbitrary circuits from LWE, secure against any polynomial number of key queries, with ciphertext size independent of both collusion count and supported circuit size.
status: General compact FE follows from stronger obfuscation-related assumptions; bounded-collusion minimal-assumption FE has collusion-dependent ciphertexts.
why: Would enable general controlled disclosure under a conventional lattice assumption.
key_works: Garg et al. (2013/2016), [*Candidate Indistinguishability Obfuscation and Functional Encryption for all Circuits*](https://doi.org/10.1137/14095772X); Ananth–Vaikuntanathan (2019), [*Optimal Bounded-Collusion Secure Functional Encryption*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2019/314).

title: A16. Unleveled ABE from ordinary circular LWE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Obtain fully collusion-resistant ABE for unbounded-depth circuits from ordinary LWE plus conventional circular security, without evasive-circular assumptions.
status: Ordinary circular security gives unbounded-depth single-key FE, single-key ABE, and reusable garbling; full ABE and predicate encryption use evasive-circular LWE.
why: Would remove a predetermined depth ceiling without escalating to a specialized assumption.
key_works: Hsieh–Lin–Luo (2023/2025), [*Attribute-Based Encryption for Circuits of Unbounded Depth from Lattices: Garbled Circuits of Optimal Size, Laconic Functional Evaluation, and More*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/1716).

title: A17. Simultaneously optimal circuit-ABE components
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Make the cryptographic portions of public parameters, ciphertexts, and secret keys simultaneously independent of policy size and depth under ordinary LWE, allowing public descriptions externally.
status: Polynomial-in-security-parameter keys are known; small keys alone do not give the full simultaneous compactness target.
why: Optimizing one component can merely move the cost into another.
key_works: Cini–Wee (2023/2025), [*ABE for Circuits with poly(\(\lambda\))-Sized Keys from LWE*](https://doi.org/10.1137/24M1636162); Hsieh–Lin–Luo (2023/2025), [*Attribute-Based Encryption for Circuits of Unbounded Depth from Lattices*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/1716).

title: A18. Fully attribute-hiding predicate encryption for circuits
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Construct circuit predicate encryption from LWE that hides challenge attributes even from authorized keys whenever the authorized outputs agree.
status: Circuit predicate encryption with weak attribute hiding is established; security restricted to keys rejecting both attributes does not meet the stronger target.
why: Authorization should not reveal unrelated attributes of encrypted data.
key_works: Gorbunov–Vaikuntanathan–Wee (2015), [*Predicate Encryption for Circuits from LWE*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-48000-7_25).

title: A19. General registered FE from ordinary LWE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Construct fully collusion-resistant registered FE for circuits from LWE, with independently generated user keys and succinct aggregation by an untrusted curator.
status: General constructions use powerful primitives; recent lattice results cover pseudorandom functionalities or bounded-collusion settings under additional assumptions.
why: Would remove central secret-key generation from general functional encryption.
key_works: Pal–Schädlich–Tairi (2025), [*Registered Functional Encryption for Pseudorandom Functionalities from Lattices*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/967); Zhang–Chen–He–Zhang (2024/2025), [*Bounded Collusion-Resistant Registered Functional Encryption for Circuits*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1572).

title: A21. Depth-independent registered ABE from succinct LWE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Remove circuit-depth factors from registered circuit ABE based on succinct LWE, retaining succinct parameters and unbounded polynomially many users.
status: Wee–Wu achieve \(\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,d,\log N)\)-size components; depth-independent alternatives use stronger machinery.
why: Would avoid choosing resource budgets around the deepest future policy.
key_works: Wee–Wu (2025), [*Unbounded Distributed Broadcast Encryption and Registered ABE from Succinct LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1039).

title: A23. Remove random oracles from succinct registered circuit ABE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Achieve the nearly optimal registered-circuit-ABE parameter envelope from succinct LWE in the plain model, supporting unbounded polynomially many independent user keys.
status: The relevant 2025 constructions use random oracles; removing depth dependence is a separate problem.
why: Would replace idealized hashing with a concrete standard-model foundation.
key_works: Wee–Wu (2025), [*Unbounded Distributed Broadcast Encryption and Registered ABE from Succinct LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1039); Champion–Hsieh–Wu (2025), [*Registered ABE and Adaptively-Secure Broadcast Encryption from Succinct LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/044).

title: A25. Malicious-client-secure circuit multi-client ABE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Obtain adaptive multi-client circuit ABE tolerating substantial malicious-client participation, with independent encryption and secure binding of ciphertext combinations to identifiers.
status: The 2025 introduction provides circuit constructions with limited adaptivity and corrupted-client security.
why: Independently supplied encrypted inputs should not create cross-session or substitution attacks.
key_works: Cini–Lai–Woo (2025), [*Lattice-based Multi-Authority/Client Attribute-based Encryption for Circuits*](https://cic.iacr.org/p/1/4/1).

title: A27. General multi-input FE from ordinary LWE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Construct compact multi-input FE for arbitrary circuits from LWE, supporting repeated ciphertexts and security for all authorized cross-combinations.
status: General multi-input FE exists from powerful obfuscation assumptions; weaker-assumption results restrict functionality or security.
why: Enables controlled computation over independently encrypted data from multiple sources.
key_works: Goldwasser et al. (2014), [*Multi-input Functional Encryption*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-55220-5_32).

title: A30. Witness encryption for NP from ordinary LWE
open: Construct polynomial-time WE for all NP from ordinary LWE, without evasive-LWE hypotheses.
status: Open since WE’s 2013 introduction. Direct lattice candidates use evasive assumptions; recent generic-group results address a different model.
why: Would provide encrypt-to-condition functionality under a central post-quantum assumption.
key_works: Tsabary (2022), [*Candidate Witness Encryption from Lattice Techniques*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-15802-5_19); Vaikuntanathan–Wee–Wichs (2022), [*Witness Encryption and Null-IO from Evasive LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1140).

title: A34. Succinct WE from ordinary iO
open: From ordinary iO and standard auxiliaries, obtain cryptographic ciphertext length \(\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,|x|,\log|C|,\log m)\) for verification circuit \(C\) and witness bound \(m\), with public descriptions external.
status: Ordinary WE follows from iO; the stronger succinctness target currently uses stronger obfuscation or extraction notions.
why: Would separate ciphertext cost from witness and verification complexity.
key_works: Devadas–Jain–Waters–Wu (2025), [*Succinct Witness Encryption for Batch Languages and Applications*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/944).

title: A35. Bootstrapping exponentially efficient WE
open: Determine whether nontrivially exponentially efficient witness encryption can be generically amplified to polynomial-time WE under ordinary auxiliary assumptions.
status: Subexponential LWE gives encryption time roughly \(2^{m/2}\) for \(m\)-bit witnesses; no general XWE-to-WE analogue of XiO amplification follows.
why: Could convert a modest exponential improvement into a foundational construction.
key_works: Brakerski–Jain–Komargodski–Passelègue–Wichs (2017/2018), [*Non-Trivial Witness Encryption and Null-iO from Standard Assumptions*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/874).

title: A37. Standard-model WE for Schnorr-signature conditions
open: For a fixed Schnorr signature and hash instantiation, construct efficient condition encryption with a standard-model reduction and adaptive security before the required signature is issued.
status: Proposed specific target. Algebraic special-purpose WE and composable gadgets exist; ordinary false-instance WE does not itself protect true signature-existence statements.
why: Would support release tied to a familiar signature ecosystem with precisely stated security.
key_works: Garg–Hajiabadi–Kolonelos–Kothapalli–Policharla (2025), [*A Framework for Witness Encryption from Linearly Verifiable SNARKs and Applications*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1364).

title: A38. Succinct batch WE for general monotone circuit policies
open: From plain WE and conventional auxiliaries, encrypt to arbitrary monotone circuits over \(K\) NP instances with cryptographic payload polynomial in \(\lambda\), one-instance complexity, and \(\log K\).
status: CNF/DNF policies follow from weaker tools; broader bounded-space policies use iO. Public policy descriptions remain external.
why: Would compress complex conditions involving many independent pieces of evidence.
key_works: Devadas–Jain–Waters–Wu (2025), [*Succinct Witness Encryption for Batch Languages and Applications*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/944).

title: A40. Witness PRFs from plain witness encryption
open: Construct general NP witness PRFs from plain WE plus OWFs or LWE in the standard model, or prove a precise separation.
status: Witness PRFs imply WE and support additional applications; the reverse implication is not established by the original theory or recent WE constructions.
why: Would turn condition-based encryption into reusable condition-based pseudorandomness.
key_works: Zhandry (2014/2016), [*How to Avoid Obfuscation Using Witness PRFs*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/301).

title: A44. Adaptive NP SNARGs from polynomial-security iO
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Derive adaptively sound NP SNARGs from polynomially secure iO and OWFs, eliminating subexponential hardness from the implication.
status: Waters–Wu’s 2025 theorem establishes the implication using subexponentially secure iO and OWFs without an extra algebraic assumption.
why: Would reduce the hardness needed for broadly adaptive succinct verification.
key_works: Waters–Wu (2024/2025), [*A Pure Indistinguishability Obfuscation Approach to Adaptively-Sound SNARGs for NP*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/933).

title: A48. Function-statistically-binding commitments from LWE
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Construct succinct function vector commitments with the function statistical binding needed by shadow PCPs from ordinary LWE or comparably conventional assumptions.
status: Guan–Yogev’s 2026 revision instantiates Micali’s SNARG assuming LWE plus these commitments and identifies weaker-assumption commitments as a remaining target.
why: Could remove a specialized assumption from a central route to succinct arguments.
key_works: Guan–Yogev (2025/2026), [*Micali’s SNARG, Function Vector Commitments, and Fiat–Shamir*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2328).

title: A50. Amplifying mild succinctness without knowledge extraction
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Generically amplify mildly succinct, ordinarily sound noninteractive arguments into fully succinct SNARGs without assuming knowledge soundness.
status: The 2025 “Boosting SNARKs” theorem uses a SNARK as its starting object; ordinary soundness is a separate target.
why: Would show that compact verification can amplify without a witness-extraction premise.
key_works: Cheng–Goyal (2025), [*Boosting SNARKs and Rate-1 Barrier in Arguments of Knowledge*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ICALP.2025.56).

title: A52. The unrestricted one-group-element SNARG boundary
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Extend one-element proof lower bounds to broader verifier classes, or construct a SNARG outside the currently excluded classes.
status: Existing lower bounds apply in Maurer GGM+ROM under natural verifier restrictions and OWFs; they are not fully unrestricted impossibility theorems.
why: Would identify the true minimum size of algebraic succinct proofs.
key_works: Arnon–Dujmovic–Yogev (2025/2026), [*Pairing-Based SNARGs with Two Group Elements*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2160); Barta–Ishai–Ostrovsky–Wu (2020), [*On Succinct Arguments and Witness Encryption from Groups*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1319).

title: E02. Negligible-error two-source extraction at polylogarithmic entropy
open: Construct explicit two-source extractors with \(k=\operatorname{polylog}(n)\) entropy and error \(n^{-\omega(1)}\), ideally \(2^{-k^c}\) for constant \(c>0\).
status: Low-entropy constant-error advances do not give this guarantee; known low-error constructions require substantially more entropy.
why: Cryptographic applications often need negligible rather than constant or inverse-polynomial error.
key_works: Chattopadhyay–Zuckerman (2016/2019), [*Explicit Two-Source Extractors and Resilient Functions*](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2019/189-3/p01); Doron–Fridman (2025), [*Bit-Fixing Extractors for Almost-Logarithmic Entropy*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.APPROX/RANDOM.2025.33).

title: E04. Bit-fixing extraction at the sharp low-entropy boundary
open: Remove remaining polylogarithmic overhead in the entropy requirement for explicit oblivious bit-fixing extractors, retaining long output and low error in feasible parameter regimes.
status: Doron–Fridman achieve almost-logarithmic entropy with long output and low error in 2025.
why: Bit-fixing sources model randomness with unknown deterministic coordinates.
key_works: Doron–Fridman (2025), [*Bit-Fixing Extractors for Almost-Logarithmic Entropy*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.APPROX/RANDOM.2025.33).

title: E05. Explicit low-degree sumset extractors near random-polynomial bounds
open: Deterministically construct low-degree polynomials matching the entropy/error regimes achieved by random polynomials on sumset sources.
status: The 2025 random-polynomial framework gives strong existence theorems; deterministic explicitness remains distinct.
why: Would translate algebraic existence into usable low-complexity extractors.
key_works: Alrabiah–Goodman–Mosheiff–Ribeiro (2025), [*Low-Degree Polynomials Are Good Extractors*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.APPROX/RANDOM.2025.38).

title: E09. Samplable-source extraction from weaker circuit hardness
open: Replace nondeterministic exponential circuit-hardness assumptions in multiplicative-error extraction for samplable sources by deterministic circuit hardness.
status: Shaltiel’s 2025 analysis explains why current techniques generate pseudorandomness against nondeterministic circuits and therefore use stronger premises.
why: Would weaken the complexity assumptions needed to clean algorithmically generated randomness.
key_works: Shaltiel (2025), [*Multiplicative Extractors for Samplable Distributions*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.22).

title: P01. Polylogarithmic two-server information-theoretic PIR
open: Construct two-server PIR for arbitrary N-bit databases with polylogarithmic total communication and information-theoretic single-server privacy, without free correlated setup.
status: Dvir–Gopi achieve \(\exp(O(\sqrt{\log N\log\log N}))\) communication; the gap to logarithmic lower bounds remains enormous.
why: Would enable very short private queries without computational assumptions.
key_works: Dvir–Gopi (2014/2016), [*2-Server PIR with Sub-Polynomial Communication*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.6692).

title: P02. Superlogarithmic unrestricted two-server PIR lower bounds
open: Prove superlogarithmic total-communication lower bounds allowing long answers, nonlinear protocols, and unrestricted server computation.
status: Stronger lower bounds require additional answer-size, algebraic, or probe restrictions.
why: Would reveal whether current subpolynomial upper bounds are remotely optimal.
key_works: Dvir–Gopi (2016), [*2-Server PIR with Sub-Polynomial Communication*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.6692); Kolby–Roy–Sternad–Yakoubov (2025), [*Information-Theoretic Random-Index PIR*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ITC.2025.5).

title: P04. Sublinear-time, short-message PIR with near-linear storage
open: Simultaneously achieve two-server information-theoretic privacy, \(N\operatorname{polylog}N\) storage, \(N^{1-\delta}\) online probes for fixed \(\delta>0\), and polylogarithmic communication.
status: Henzinger–Ragavan achieve quasilinear storage and sublinear probes; their stronger communication reduction invokes computational encryption.
why: Efficient communication alone does not prevent servers from scanning the database.
key_works: Henzinger–Ragavan (2026), [*Two-Server Private Information Retrieval in Sublinear Time and Quasilinear Space*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2008).

title: P10. Superpolynomial lower bounds for constant-query LDCs
open: Prove superpolynomial block length for binary locally decodable codes correcting a constant error fraction with every fixed query count, or construct a counterexample.
status: General lower bounds remain far below known superpolynomial constructions; restricted linear or low-query results do not settle all cases.
why: This coding question directly constrains information-theoretic private retrieval.
key_works: Goldreich (2024), *Lower Bounds on the Length of Locally Decodable Codes*, in [*Open Problems in Honor of Luca Trevisan*](https://doi.org/10.1145/3710795.3710799); Dvir–Gopi (2016), [*2-Server PIR with Sub-Polynomial Communication*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.6692).

title: C01. Logarithmic-overhead universal randomized compression
open: Reduce universal polynomial-time randomized-compression overhead to \(O(\log(n/\varepsilon))\), given a target description length and error \(\varepsilon\).
status: Polynomial-time constructions achieve \(O(\log m\cdot\log(n/\varepsilon))\) overhead; logarithmic overhead is known with prohibitively slow compression.
why: Would approach information-theoretic optimality without sacrificing efficient encoding.
key_works: Bauwens (2018), [*Optimal Probabilistic Polynomial Time Compression and the Slepian-Wolf Theorem: Tighter Version and Simple Proofs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.00750); Bauwens–Zimand (2019/2023), [*Universal Almost Optimal Compression and Slepian-Wolf Coding in Probabilistic Polynomial Time*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.04268).

title: G01. Ta-Shma’s polynomial quantum-error blowup conjecture
open: Prove that every classical strong extractor with m output bits and error \(\varepsilon\) is quantum-proof with error \(O(m\sqrt\varepsilon)\), allowing the stipulated logarithmic extra entropy, or give a counterexample.
status: Studied since the 2000s; general lifting bounds have exponential output-length dependence.
why: Would let broad classes of classical extractors be safely reused against quantum side information.
key_works: Berta–Fawzi–Scholz (2017), [*Quantum-proof randomness extractors via operator space theory*](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.2016.2627531), [arXiv:1409.3563](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.3563).

title: G04. Extraction with approximately Markov quantum side information
open: When \(I(X:Y\mid E)\le\delta\), determine whether exact-Markov-secure extraction incurs only a dimension-independent additional error \(f(\delta)\to0\), or construct a counterexample.
status: Explicitly raised in 2016. Approximate recoverability does not automatically reproduce exact conditional-independence structure.
why: Physical sources rarely satisfy exact mathematical independence.
key_works: Arnon-Friedman–Portmann–Scholz (2016), [*Quantum-proof multi-source randomness extractors in the Markov model*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.TQC.2016.2), [arXiv:1510.06743](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.06743).

title: G09. Quantum nonmalleable extraction with optimal seed and entropy
open: Achieve \(d=O(\log n+\log(1/\varepsilon))\), \(k=O(\log\log n+\log(1/\varepsilon))\), and output \(\Omega(k)\) against quantum side information and admissible seed tampering.
status: Classical constructions reach this target; checked quantum constructions retain polylogarithmic seed and entropy requirements.
why: Would make active quantum privacy amplification nearly entropy optimal.
key_works: Boddu–Jain–Kapshikar (2021/2024), [*Quantum secure non-malleable-extractors*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.03097); Li (2023), [*Two Source Extractors for Asymptotically Optimal Entropy, and (Many) More*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.06802).

title: G10. Two-round quantum privacy amplification with optimal loss
open: From \(H_{\min}(X\mid E)\ge k\), obtain efficient two-round active privacy amplification outputting \(k-O(\log\log n+s)\) bits with error \(2^{-s}\) for \(s\le ck\).
status: Quantum two-round feasibility is established, but checked constructions retain roughly half the entropy; classical protocols reach the stronger target.
why: Would preserve scarce quantum-secure entropy under an actively attacked communication channel.
key_works: Boddu–Jain–Kapshikar (2021/2024), [*Quantum secure non-malleable-extractors*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.03097); Li (2023), [*Two Source Extractors for Asymptotically Optimal Entropy, and (Many) More*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.06802).

title: G11. Explicit seeded condensers with coefficient one on log error
subfield: Condensers, online adversaries, and entropy deficiency
open: Match existential lossless-condenser parameters \(d=\log(n-k)+\log(1/\varepsilon)+O(1)\) and \(m=k+d+\log(1/\varepsilon)+O(1)\).
status: Random functions achieve this leading error dependence; general explicit constructions remain weaker.
why: The coefficient of \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\) controls several downstream seedless-condensing constructions.
key_works: Goodman–Li–Zuckerman (2024), [*Improved Condensers for Chor-Goldreich Sources*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.08142).

title: G12. Constant-factor gap loss for low-entropy Chor–Goldreich sources
subfield: Condensers, online adversaries, and entropy deficiency
open: Condense n-bit blocks with at least \(n^{0.99}\) conditional min-entropy each to rate at least 0.9, with deficiency \(O(n-n^{0.99}+\log(1/\varepsilon))\).
status: Explicit low-entropy condensation is established; current constructions can enlarge the inherited deficiency by a polynomial factor.
why: Would prevent repeated weak-source processing from wasting most usable entropy.
key_works: Goodman–Li–Zuckerman (2024), [*Improved Condensers for Chor-Goldreich Sources*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.08142).

title: G13. Linear entropy deficiency for unpredictable sources
subfield: Condensers, online adversaries, and entropy deficiency
open: Improve online condensation of \((\delta,\rho)\)-unpredictable sources to rate \(1-O(\rho)\), with \(\Omega(\delta dt)\) output and the stipulated polynomial-in-\(\rho\) error.
status: Doron–Moshkovitz–Oh–Zuckerman explicitly conjecture this improvement; their random-walk construction gives rate \(1-\rho^{1/C}\).
why: Would sharply improve the quality of randomness extracted from occasionally predictable blocks.
key_works: Doron–Moshkovitz–Oh–Zuckerman (2025), [*Online Condensing of Unpredictable Sources via Random Walks*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.30).

title: G15. The online bit-fixing non-condensing conjecture
subfield: Condensers, online adversaries, and entropy deficiency
open: Resolve whether deterministic condensation can nontrivially raise the entropy rate of online nonoblivious bit-fixing sources in the constant-rate regime, allowing small smoothing error.
status: Zero-error obstructions are known; the authors explicitly conjecture a remaining non-condensing barrier.
why: Would explain a fundamental difference between one-bit and longer-block contributions.
key_works: Chattopadhyay–Gurumukhani–Ringach–Servedio (2026), [*Condensing and Extracting Against Online Adversaries*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04115), open-problems section.

title: G18. Seedless samplable condensing beyond black-box assumptions
subfield: Condensers, online adversaries, and entropy deficiency
open: Construct seedless condensers for general efficient samplers from established assumptions such as LWE using non-black-box techniques, matching specialized-assumption parameters.
status: Freitag–Silbak–Wichs give near-optimal specialized-hashing constructions and a black-box barrier for standard game-based assumptions.
why: Would give a conventional foundation for deterministic improvement of algorithmically generated randomness.
key_works: Freitag–Silbak–Wichs (2025), [*Seedless Condensers for Efficiently Samplable Sources*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1783).

title: G19. Quasilinear Raz extraction without auxiliary length restrictions
open: Extend quasilinear Raz extraction throughout its original asymmetric source-length regime, removing \(n_2\le n_1/2\) and associated auxiliary-parameter restrictions.
status: The 2025 implementation already runs in \(O(n_1\log^2 n_1)\) on its supported parameters; broadening that range is explicitly open.
why: Would make fast extraction available for more realistic unequal-source configurations.
key_works: Foreman–Wooltorton–Milner–Curchod (2025), [*An efficient construction of Raz’s two-source randomness extractor with improved parameters*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.15547).

title: G20. Ordinary-to-seedless-nonmalleable extractor conversion
open: Convert arbitrary two-source or affine extractors into seedless nonmalleable extractors with polynomial error loss, constant-factor entropy overhead, and constant-fraction output.
status: Explicitly asked in 2024. Strong dedicated constructions do not supply a generic conversion.
why: Would allow advances in ordinary extraction to transfer automatically to tamper-resistant randomness.
key_works: Li–Zhong (2024), [*Two-Source and Affine Non-Malleable Extractors for Small Entropy*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ICALP.2024.108).

title: G21. Negligible-error two-source nonmalleability at polylogarithmic entropy
open: Extract nonconstant output with error \(n^{-\omega(1)}\) from two polylogarithmic-entropy sources against separate tampering functions, at least one fixed-point-free.
status: The 2024 constructions achieve polynomial error with long output or constant output at logarithmic entropy.
why: Would support negligible-error tamper resistance from extremely weak independent sources.
key_works: Li–Zhong (2024), [*Two-Source and Affine Non-Malleable Extractors for Small Entropy*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ICALP.2024.108).

title: G24. Short-seed linear extractors with linear output
open: Construct strong extractors linear in the source for each fixed seed, with \(d=O(\log(n/\varepsilon))\), \(m=\Omega(k)\), and \(k\ge C\log(n/\varepsilon)\) throughout the low-entropy regime.
status: Known linear constructions trade seed length against output length; unrestricted seeded extraction does not settle this linearity-constrained target.
why: Linearity enables efficient integration with coding, sharing, and algebraic protocols.
key_works: Doron–Fridman (2025), [*Bit-Fixing Extractors for Almost-Logarithmic Entropy*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.APPROX/RANDOM.2025.33), Section 2.3.

title: G25. Optimal-order seeded extraction against unrestricted quantum information
open: Extract \(\Omega(k)\) bits with seed \(O(\log(n/\varepsilon))\) whenever \(H_{\min}(X\mid E)\ge k\ge C\log(n/\varepsilon)\), for arbitrary-dimensional quantum E.
status: Trevisan-style constructions recover nearly all entropy with longer seeds; shorter-seed results impose restrictions. The 2016 general-optimality claim was withdrawn.
why: Would match classical-order extraction parameters against unrestricted quantum storage.
key_works: De–Portmann–Vidick–Renner (2012), [*Trevisan’s Extractor in the Presence of Quantum Side Information*](https://doi.org/10.1137/100813683); Ben-Aroya–Ta-Shma (2012), [*Better short-seed quantum-proof extractors*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.3737); [withdrawn 2016 claim](https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.04194).

title: R3-005. The three-uniform hypergraph share-size gap
open: Determine the optimal worst-case total information ratio when minimal authorized sets all have size three. Improve the \(\Omega(n^{3/2})\) lower bound or \(O(n^3/\log n)\) upper bound in the long-secret regime.
status: Beimel’s 2023 lower bound reaches \(n^{3/2}\); decomposition constructions leave a polynomial gap. Large unauthorized sets are allowed, distinguishing this model from slices.
why: Measures how expensive authorization by triples can be.
key_works: Amos Beimel (2023), [*Lower Bounds for Secret-Sharing Schemes for k-Hypergraphs*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ITC.2023.16), especially the \(k=3\) case.

title: R3-008. Duality for perfect nonlinear secret sharing
open: Decide whether an access structure and its dual always have the same optimal maximum-share information ratio under perfect reconstruction and perfect privacy. A concrete unequal pair would refute the conjecture.
status: Equality holds for multilinear constructions. Csirmaz’s 2019/2021 counterexample uses almost-perfect sharing on 174 participants, leaving the perfect model unresolved.
why: Determines whether complementing an authorization policy can change its fundamental storage cost.
key_works: László Csirmaz (2019; journal 2021), [*Secret Sharing and Duality*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.13663); Applebaum–Nir (2021), [*Upslices, Downslices, and Secret-Sharing with Complexity of 1.5ⁿ*](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2021/052/).

title: R3-015. Safe two-scheme key cycles
open: For every public-key encryption scheme \(\mathrm{Enc}\), does some scheme \(\mathrm{Enc}'\) preserve \(\mathrm{Enc}\)’s security when \(\mathrm{Enc}'(sk)\) and \(\mathrm{Enc}(sk')\) are published, using independent keys?
status: Micciancio’s 2025 Conjecture 2; same-scheme cycle counterexamples do not settle it.
why: Would justify heterogeneous key cycles used in composability transformations.
key_works: Daniele Micciancio (2025), [*Fully Composable Homomorphic Encryption*](https://cic.iacr.org/p/2/1/1), DOI:10.62056/ak5wl86bm, Conjecture 2.

title: R3-016. Full composability from ordinary FHE alone
open: Does ordinary fully homomorphic encryption imply fully composable homomorphic encryption without a circular-security hypothesis?
status: Explicitly unresolved in Micciancio (2025); fresh-ciphertext correctness is insufficient.
why: Would close a gap between foundational FHE definitions and arbitrary composition.
key_works: Daniele Micciancio (2025), [*Fully Composable Homomorphic Encryption*](https://cic.iacr.org/p/2/1/1), DOI:10.62056/ak5wl86bm.

title: R3-017. Unbounded-circuit KDM security from ordinary LWE
open: Construct public-key encryption from ordinary LWE secure for every polynomial-size key-dependent-message circuit, with the scheme fixed independently of the circuit-size bound and number of keys. Permit adaptive circuit choices.
status: The distinction dates to 2010. Kitagawa–Matsuda’s 2020 amplification supports arbitrary numbers of keys but still requires an a priori circuit-size bound; circular-secure, circuit-private FHE gives the unbounded form under additional assumptions.
why: Would remove a predetermined complexity ceiling from applications encrypting key-dependent data.
key_works: Boaz Barak, Iftach Haitner, Dennis Hofheinz and Yuval Ishai (2010), [*Bounded Key-Dependent Message Security*](https://iftachh.github.io/MyHomepage/papers/BoundedKDM/boundedkdm.pdf); Fuyuki Kitagawa and Takahiro Matsuda (2020), [*Circular Security Is Complete for KDM Security*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1060); Benny Applebaum (2014), [*Key-Dependent Message Security: Generic Amplification and Completeness*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00145-013-9149-6).

title: R3-018. Collision resistance at algebraic degree two
open: Construct a shrinking collision-resistant hash family whose coordinates are degree-two polynomials over \(\mathbb F_2\), or prove that every efficiently sampled family admits efficient collision finding. A specially chosen hard distribution of quadratic maps is allowed.
status: Explicitly open since 2017. Degree three is achievable under codeword-hardness assumptions; random quadratic maps provide universal one-way hashing under a quadratic-system assumption but are not collision resistant.
why: Determines whether a single multiplication layer can support collision resistance.
key_works: Benny Applebaum, Naama Haramaty-Krasne, Yuval Ishai, Eyal Kushilevitz and Vinod Vaikuntanathan (2017), [*Low-Complexity Cryptographic Hash Functions*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ITCS.2017.7).

title: R3-022. Collusion-resistant private puncturing from DCR
open: Extend privately constrained PRFs based on decisional composite residuosity to polynomially many colluding constrained keys, hiding punctured points under a multi-key privacy definition. Retain an exponentially large domain without stronger obfuscation or FHE assumptions.
status: Proposed extension of a 2025 frontier: Behera–Meyer–Orlandi–Roy–Scholl achieve single-key selective security for polynomially bounded Waring-rank predicates, including puncturing.
why: Enables multiple independent delegations using one algebraic PRF family.
key_works: Amik Raj Behera, Pierre Meyer, Claudio Orlandi, Lawrence Roy and Peter Scholl (2025), [*Privately Constrained PRFs from DCR: Puncturing and Bounded Waring Rank*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/230).

title: R3-024. Adaptive registered attribute-weighted sums with unbounded inputs
open: Construct registered FE for attribute-weighted sums with access control and an a priori unbounded number of attribute-value pairs, allowing adaptive challenge attributes, registrations and corruptions. Retain ciphertext compactness independent of public-input length under standard pairing assumptions.
status: Pal–Schädlich (2026) achieve adaptive IND security for one input pair. Their unbounded-input construction requires challenge attributes, registered functions and corrupted users to be declared upfront; closing that gap is the proposed target.
why: Supports changing encrypted records without advance knowledge of future access patterns.
key_works: Tapas Pal and Robert Schädlich (2026), [*Compact Registered Functional Encryption for Attribute-Weighted Sums with Access Control*](https://publikationen.bibliothek.kit.edu/1000194419), DOI:10.1007/978-3-032-26737-5_11.

title: R3-032. Adaptive deletion for arbitrary monotone access structures
open: Construct information-theoretic secret sharing with adaptive certified deletion for every efficiently representable monotone access structure. The adversary may corrupt and delete shares sequentially, while its currently undeleted shares remain unauthorized.
status: Explicit since Bartusek–Raizes (2024). Threshold structures are achieved; their general-access construction has no-signaling security. Katz–Sela (2025) reiterate the privately verifiable information-theoretic question.
why: Supports deletion policies based on complex organizational authorization rules.
key_works: James Bartusek and Justin Raizes (2024), [*Secret Sharing with Certified Deletion*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.08117); Jonathan Katz and Ben Sela (2025), [*Secret Sharing with Publicly Verifiable Deletion*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1596), [EUROCRYPT slides](https://iacr.org/submit/files/slides/2025/eurocrypt/eurocrypt2025/234/234_slides.pdf).

title: R3-034. Threshold signing keys with certified deletion
open: Construct threshold signatures whose quantum signing-key shares can be certifiably deleted, preserving unforgeability against sequential compromises whenever too few undeleted shares have accumulated. Authorized parties must still produce independently combinable partial signatures.
status: Explicitly posed in 2024 and Raizes’s 2025 thesis. Deletion of threshold secret shares does not itself provide reusable signing on protected shares.
why: Makes retirement of distributed signing authority cryptographically checkable.
key_works: Bartusek–Raizes (2024), [*Secret Sharing with Certified Deletion*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.08117); Justin Raizes (2025), [*Quantum Approaches to Verifiable Deletion*](https://csd.cmu.edu/sites/default/files/phd-thesis/CMU-CS-25-107.pdf), §11.4; Yvo Desmedt and Yair Frankel (1989/1990), [*Threshold Cryptosystems*](https://doi.org/10.1007/0-387-34805-0_28).

title: R3-036. Public deletion verification for CE-NIZK without iO
open: Obtain statistically sound NP NIZK with publicly verifiable deletion and certified-everlasting zero knowledge without assuming indistinguishability obfuscation.
status: Explicit in Pappu’s September 2026 revision; LWE constructions provide private verification, while a coset-state/iO route is suggested.
why: Supports independent deletion audits.
key_works: Nikhil Pappu (2025; revised 2026), [*Certified-Everlasting Quantum NIZK Proofs*](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.13628v4), §2.7.

title: R3-043. Plain-model certified-deniable signatures beyond black-box simulation
open: Construct plain-model signatures with certified deniability using a non-black-box simulator, or extend the impossibility to such simulators. After deletion, retained evidence must be simulatable without the signature beyond independently available prior information.
status: Çakan–Goyal–Raizes give QROM constructions and a plain-model black-box simulation barrier; the stronger impossibility is not established.
why: Determines whether a verifier can credibly erase evidence of a signed interaction without an idealized oracle.
key_works: Alper Çakan, Vipul Goyal and Justin Raizes (2024; revised 2025; CRYPTO 2026), [*How to Delete Without a Trace: Certified Deniability in a Quantum World*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1832); Justin Raizes (2025), [*Quantum Approaches to Verifiable Deletion*](https://csd.cmu.edu/sites/default/files/phd-thesis/CMU-CS-25-107.pdf), Part III.

title: R3-047. Simultaneous-message QKD with full everlasting security
open: Obtain QKD with two simultaneous messages and standard everlasting security, including agreement-or-abort under active attacks.
status: Explicit in 2025; known simultaneous-message security is a conditional search guarantee. Four messages over two rounds achieve full security.
why: Enables independent sending.
key_works: Alex B. Grilo, Giulio Malavolta, Michael Walter and Tianwei Zhang (2025; proceedings 2026), [*Computational Monogamy of Entanglement and Non-Interactive Quantum Key Distribution*](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.00791v1), §1.3.

title: R3-048. Positive key rate in two-round EPR-based QKD
open: Achieve standard everlasting security and \(\Omega(n)\) secret key bits from \(n\) transmitted qubits in two rounds, using EPR pairs and single-qubit measurements.
status: The 2025 computational-monogamy protocol achieves two rounds; positive key rate is explicitly left open.
why: Improves usable key yield.
key_works: Grilo, Malavolta, Walter and Zhang (2025; proceedings 2026), [*Computational Monogamy of Entanglement and Non-Interactive Quantum Key Distribution*](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.00791v1), §1.3.

title: R3-049. Computational monogamy with arbitrary efficient Bob measurements
open: In computational monogamy with an initially computationally hidden BB84 basis, allow Bob any efficient basis-dependent POVM while Charlie remains unbounded; bound their joint guessing probability negligibly.
status: Explicit in 2025; the theorem requires Bob’s prescribed basis measurement.
why: Handles adversarial recipient processing.
key_works: Grilo, Malavolta, Walter and Zhang (2025), [*Computational Monogamy of Entanglement and Non-Interactive Quantum Key Distribution*](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.00791v1), §1.3.

title: R3-050. Computational monogamy with two unbounded measurement stages
open: Strengthen the same game to arbitrary unbounded POVMs for both Bob and Charlie after efficient state preparation with a computationally hidden basis.
status: Explicit in 2025; even allowing only efficient arbitrary Bob measurements remains unresolved.
why: Separates preparation and measurement complexity.
key_works: Grilo, Malavolta, Walter and Zhang (2025), [*Computational Monogamy of Entanglement and Non-Interactive Quantum Key Distribution*](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.00791v1), §1.3.

title: R3-051. Two-message QKD in the qubit-by-qubit model
open: Construct two-message everlasting-secure QKD whose states and operations follow the qubit-by-qubit model, without coherent joint processing of polynomial-size quantum registers.
status: Malavolta–Walter explicitly pose this restriction in 2023/2024; their OWF-based two-message construction uses many-qubit superpositions.
why: Makes minimal interaction compatible with simpler quantum optical hardware.
key_works: Giulio Malavolta and Michael Walter (2023; revised 2024), [*Robust Quantum Public-Key Encryption with Applications to Quantum Key Distribution*](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2304.02999), §1.3.

title: R3-057. Statistical randomized encodings of degree two
open: Decide whether every finite Boolean function has a statistical randomized encoding whose output coordinates are degree-at-most-two polynomials over \(\mathbb F_2\) in input and random bits.
status: Degree three suffices; perfect-privacy lower bounds do not settle the statistical relaxation. This boundary is explicitly identified in the literature.
why: Would lower the algebraic complexity of information-theoretic secure computation.
key_works: Benny Applebaum (2017), [*Garbled Circuits as Randomized Encodings of Functions: A Primer*](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2017/067/), §4.1; Shai Halevi, Yuval Ishai, Eyal Kushilevitz and Tal Rabin (2023), [*Additive Randomized Encodings and Their Applications*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/870).

title: R3-058. Statistical randomized encodings of locality three
open: Decide whether every finite Boolean function admits a statistically private encoding in which each output bit depends on at most three input-or-randomness bits.
status: Locality four is achievable; locality two is insufficient in general. The intermediate statistical case remains unresolved in the cited treatment.
why: Measures the smallest local operation supporting general private encodings.
key_works: Benny Applebaum (2017), [*Garbled Circuits as Randomized Encodings of Functions: A Primer*](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2017/067/), §4.1.

title: R3-061. One-round framing-free distributed ZK
open: In the ideal-coin-tossing model, obtain a one-round information-theoretic distributed ZK proof with strong completeness against malicious verifiers, or prove two rounds necessary. Retain verification communication independent of statement circuit size.
status: Hazay–Venkitasubramaniam–Weiss obtain two rounds for appropriately robustly encoded statements and \(k>6t+2\); they explicitly leave round optimality open.
why: Makes private input certification compatible with one upload followed by verification.
key_works: Carmit Hazay, Muthuramakrishnan Venkitasubramaniam and Mor Weiss (2023; journal 2026), [*Your Reputation’s Safe with Me: Framing-Free Distributed Zero-Knowledge Proofs*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00145-026-09576-7), §1.3.

title: R3-063. Polynomial-loss reduction from local sources to local NOBF sources
open: Reduce every \(d\)-local source of min-entropy \(k\) to a distribution exponentially close to a mixture of \(d\)-local nonoblivious bit-fixing sources retaining \(\Omega(k/\operatorname{poly}(d))\) entropy, or prove this impossible. Each original output bit depends on at most \(d\) uniform input bits.
status: Explicitly posed in 2022. The known reduction retains \(\Omega(k/(2^d d^2))\) entropy.
why: Extends local-source extraction to growing locality.
key_works: Omar Alrabiah, Eshan Chattopadhyay, Jesse Goodman, Xin Li and João Ribeiro (2022), [*Low-Degree Polynomials Extract from Local Sources*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.13725), Theorem 2 and §1.2; DOI:10.4230/LIPIcs.ICALP.2022.10.

title: R3-064. Sharp low-weight Chevalley–Warning bounds for quadratic systems
open: Determine the sharp \(n,m\)-dependent upper bound on the minimum Hamming weight of a nonzero common zero of \(m\) quadratic polynomials over \(\mathbb F_2\), assuming all vanish at zero and \(2m<n\). Can a linear-in-\(m\) bound remain necessary when \(n/m\) grows?
status: The 2022 low-weight Chevalley–Warning theorem gives \(O(m)\); tightness for quadratic systems remains explicitly unresolved.
why: Controls algebraic obstructions to extraction and sparse polynomial-system solutions.
key_works: Alrabiah, Chattopadhyay, Goodman, Li and Ribeiro (2022), [*Low-Degree Polynomials Extract from Local Sources*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.13725), Theorem 4 and §1.2.

title: R3-066. Exponentially small error for random constant-degree sumset extractors
open: Prove the conjecture that most degree-\(d\) polynomials extract from sumset sources at entropy \(k=Cdn^{C/d}\) with exponentially small error, even for fixed \(d\). A concrete milestone is error \(2^{-n^{\Omega(1)}}\) at a small constant entropy rate.
status: Posed in 2025. For even \(d\), the current general bound requires \(k=O(d(n/\varepsilon^2)^{2/d})\), preventing this error regime at fixed degree.
why: Supplies strong statistical security without increasing algebraic degree with the error parameter.
key_works: Alrabiah, Goodman, Mosheiff and Ribeiro (2025), [*Low-Degree Polynomials Are Good Extractors*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.10297), Theorem 2 and §7.

title: R3-073. Lifting group-product generators to arbitrary group-valued blocks
open: Extend the near-optimal group-product-to-block-product reduction to \(\prod_i h_i(x_{I_i})\), with arbitrary group-valued maps on disjoint blocks. Preserve near-optimal seed dependence on block width, block count and error for a fixed noncommutative mixing group such as the quaternions.
status: The 2025 reduction treats \(g_i^{f_i(x_{I_i})}\) with Boolean \(f_i\); extending the block’s range to the entire group is explicitly open.
why: Removes a Boolean-exponent restriction from algebraic derandomization.
key_works: Chin Ho Lee and Emanuele Viola (2025), [*Pseudorandom Bits for Non-Commutative Programs*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.9), Theorem 10 and §1.2.
